{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOV5s7_c8AAAABi9KVjg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bs-hLzhMTWCk", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bs-hL", "number": 13, "title": "Stop automatically creating Recovery save-data profiles on state load", "body": "## Goal and scope

Stop automatically creating Recovery save-data profiles when loading a save state, for both battery-backed NES cartridges and FDS games. Ordinary state loading must not clutter the user's Save data list or consume increasingly more storage.

The current behavior was introduced by #9. In [web/src/main.js](https://github.com/takahirox/nes-rust-neo/blob/5a579dc84c52559298a69511b6c1f6d62d40b403/web/src/main.js#L576-L635), restoreNativeProgress() compares live, persisted and snapshot-native bytes and preserveDisplacedProgress() creates up to two new Recovery profiles on each load. [addProfile()](https://github.com/takahirox/nes-rust-neo/blob/5a579dc84c52559298a69511b6c1f6d62d40b403/web/src/save-storage.js#L26-L35) always allocates a new ID. Repeated normal gameplay and state loads can therefore accumulate an unbounded number of profiles, including duplicate progress.

The maintainer explicitly accepts that loading an older state replaces the currently selected profile's native save data with the snapshot's data, without automatically backing up the displaced version.

- Remove automatic Recovery profile creation from the state-load path. Load restores the machine and its native progress (NES SRAM or FDS disk changes) to the current profile. Keep the current profile selected and the profile count unchanged. No extra confirmation, automatic backup slot or replacement recovery mechanism is required.
- Retain explicit New save, Duplicate current and Import save data actions for users who want independent saves or backups. Existing Recovery profiles and their attached states remain accessible and removable like other profiles; do not automatically delete or migrate them.
- Remove obsolete state-load recovery creation code, recovery-specific success messages and obsolete test expectations. Update README and save-state documentation to explain that loading a state can roll back native progress and users can explicitly duplicate/export a save first.
- Keep existing snapshot validation, normal persistence, storage-error handling and non-destructive failed-load behavior. Do not change the unrelated legacy battery-save conflict/retry mechanism, save formats, storage schema, fullscreen layout or emulator core.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Using the existing NES battery and FDS fixtures, save a state, change native progress, then load the earlier state repeatedly. Verify that the expected SRAM/disk bytes and gameplay are restored, the selected profile is unchanged and no new Recovery or other profile appears. Use focused existing browser regressions adapted to the new behavior.
- [ ] Verify an existing Recovery profile remains usable, explicit profile creation still works, and an ordinary failed required storage write does not replace the running machine. Reuse existing coverage rather than creating a new failure or viewport matrix.
- [ ] Mandatory repository CI passes on the final revision. Record concise test results and update the relevant documentation. No mandatory human confirmation is required.

Keep this a small behavioral change. Do not add backup retention, deduplication, migration, new UI, speculative concurrency handling or unrelated refactors. Once the above criteria are met and no material supported-use defect remains, complete review and merge; do not expand acceptance or repeat validation merely for additional assurance.

For implementers and reviewers, only a concrete material defect in the requested behavior or an ordinary supported workflow (e.g. failed state restoration, unintended data loss beyond the explicitly accepted rollback, or unusable save controls), or a required CI failure, is a merge blocker. Minor cosmetic/UI/UX issues, unusual viewport combinations, hypothetical compound failures and pre-existing unrelated issues must not block this change. Adjust obsolete recovery-specific assertions to the new behavior rather than expanding the layout or storage test matrix; do not waive genuine required CI failures. Once the focused criteria and final CI pass, approve, merge and close without another optional review/fix cycle.

## Post-merge verification

Confirm the Pages deployment succeeds and briefly smoke-test repeated state loading without new Recovery profiles. Record the result in the merged PR or closed Issue. Publication is not a pre-merge gate.

outputs.message: PR #14 merged into `main`, and GitHub closed Issue #13 as completed. CI and the Pages deployment passed. Two Chromium checks against the live site confirmed that repeated state loads restored NES SRAM and FDS disk progress, kept the selected profile, and created no Recovery profiles. [Results recorded on Issue #13](https://github.com/takahirox/nes-rust-neo/issues/13#issuecomment-7211245601).
